notes: SHIP v1.14.365 - OPS WALL LIVE DATA. Owner ruled SHIP-BUILD-BANNER-ROWS-SPEC section 8 IS the spec for this ship, releasing the block that had held it pending a separate web-Claude document. Requirement: the nine BUILD OPS wall cells bind to real accessors and read at render time, with an explicit empty state when there is no data - blank is never an erase - and NO SAMPLE_STATE literal reaching this file in any form. All nine are bound. WHAT EACH CELL READS, AND THE ONE PLACE THE SPEC'S WORDING HAD TO BE READ FOR INTENT RATHER THAN LETTER: section 8 says every cell 'reads phantomMaster', but only RACK MAP is Master-backed in this app (racksByCab -> cabinet count). The other eight tools keep state in their own stores: SOPS -> loadSOPs, OPTICS -> loadOpticInventory, BURNDOWN -> BD.count, AUDITS -> AUDIT.count, MANIFEST -> deploy_loadAll filtered to active/paused/complete, BLAST -> omni_getActiveDeployment then deploy_loadRacksFor, BOM -> IndexedDB. Each cell binds to the source of the tool it actually opens, because a cell that counted the Master would print a number the tool behind it does not have. The mock's own SRC provenance map labelled portmap, manifest, audits, burndown and bom as 'Master' - that is wrong for the live app, and porting it faithfully would have shipped five lying provenance labels. TWO STRUCTURAL FINDINGS THAT SHAPED THE SHIP. (1) PORT MAP HAS NO STORE AT ALL. It is a paste-and-validate tool, not a data view - there is nothing to count, and the master's cables[] array is not even persisted (PHANTOM_MASTER_STORE keeps racksByCab only, so a restored Master carries no cabling). Its cell therefore carries a permanent call to action, PASTE TO RUN. That is section 8's empty state applied honestly, not a gap in the binding. (2) BOM IS ASYNC. It lives in IndexedDB while every other source is synchronous localStorage, so it cannot be read in a synchronous render pass. It paints an em-dash (pending) first and resolves in, guarded by a generation token that drops a late resolve if the wall has been re-opened since. It deliberately does NOT paint 'NO DATA' while the read is in flight, because asserting no-data before the answer returns is itself a fabricated state. TWO MISLEADING-NUMBER TRAPS CAUGHT BY READING THE TOOLS FIRST. BD.renderList filters !archived and labels the result 'active'; a raw length would have counted every job the tool has already put away, so BD.count applies the same filter and the cell agrees with the tool it opens. AUDIT.renderList shows load() unfiltered, so AUDIT.count is deliberately unfiltered for the same reason. The counts were matched to each tool's OWN definition rather than to a single convenient rule. ZERO AND UNAVAILABLE BOTH RENDER THE EMPTY MARKER: both mean 'nothing here' to a gloved tech and neither may be dressed up as a measurement. Markers are per-cell and several are a call to action rather than a shortage: SCAN TO SEED (optics, the exact wording the mock used for its honest optics:null case), PASTE TO RUN (portmap), NO MASTER (rackmap), NO DEPLOY (blast), NO DATA elsewhere. ENCAPSULATION: BD and AUDIT each gained a read-only count() on their public return rather than having the wall read BURNDOWN_KEY or AUDIT's KEY literal directly. AUDIT's key is a literal local to its closure, so the alternative was duplicating a storage-key string outside the module that owns it. Both additions are additive; no existing behaviour changed. DEGRADATION IS DELIBERATE AND DOCUMENTED: a stat that throws downgrades that ONE cell to its empty marker and console.warns. The wall still opens and all nine doors still tap, so the readout is an enhancement over a control that already works - it warns rather than toasting, because a toast for a cosmetic degradation trains the operator to ignore toasts. Only a missing wall host, which is a structural bug, is loud (warn + toast). This is a deliberate reading of the No Silent Failures rule, whose root cause was DEAD TAPS: no tap in this wall can be dead, and none is. A11Y: aria-label overrides a control's text content for a screen reader, so each cell's label is re-composed on paint as base + readout; without that the count would be visible but unspoken. The base label is cached in JS on first paint, so no extra markup attribute was needed. NO LAYOUT SHIFT: the value line was sized so the cell does not grow - four children total 35.2px + 3x6px gaps + 20px padding = 73.2px, still under the existing 88px min-height floor. The wall's geometry is byte-for-byte what .359 shipped. SECTION 8 COMPLIANCE VERIFIED MECHANICALLY: every one of the mock's sample values - the port pair, the manifest pair, the verified count, the three serials, the parts/open pair and the PDU percentage - was grepped against THIS SHIP'S ADDED LINES in dct-ios.html, not the whole file, which contains such digits innocently. None appears, in code or in comment. The values themselves are deliberately NOT enumerated in this note either: the .359 ship had to reword its own comments for exactly this reason, and the list belongs in the gate, which is not shipped, rather than in the repo. The mock's per-cell mini-visualisations (fill grids, bars, sparklines) were NOT ported: they were designed for the mock's larger cell, and the 3x3 wall that actually shipped gives each cell about 108x88px on a 390px phone. Cramming a sparkline in there fails Design Law 5 and the Cold Aisle Filter. One readable line per cell is the form that survives the aisle. GATES: three-stamp lockstep; node --check on all four inline blocks + sw.js; CSS brace balance across all style blocks; ops-cell token count still exactly 9 (the owner's standing acceptance check); all nine rd_openOpsTool handlers byte-unchanged; #work-grid is display:none outside body.rd so ?legacy=1 cannot reach any of this. DEVICE-VERIFY: (1) badge reads v1.14.365. (2) BUILD > tap OPS: the wall opens as before and every cell now carries a readout line under its label. (3) Cells with data show a count; cells without show a dimmed marker, never a blank. With no Master loaded RACK MAP reads NO MASTER; PORT MAP always reads PASTE TO RUN. (4) ALL NINE CELLS MUST STILL TAP THROUGH to their tool - the readout must never cost a door. (5) Load a Master and re-open the wall: RACK MAP's cabinet count appears without a reload, because the wall reads on every open. (6) ?legacy=1 unchanged. ROLLBACK: revert this commit - the wall returns to static labels with every door intact.
